We need propose retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1

We need to produce JSON route with type mol root, children reaction nodes etc. Need to select appropriate templates. We can search for templates matching functional group transformations: likely steps: 1) SN2 to attach side chain? The target has a side chain: Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3 attached to N of triazine? Actually structure: COc1cccc(NC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N)c1. Contains anisole ring with amide linking to a triazine (c2nnn...). The triazine has a substituent Cc3... (benzyl attached to heterocycle). That benzyl has a side chain CN4CC(F)C4 (a fluorinated azetidine? Actually N4CC(F)C4 is a 3-member? It's N-azetidine with F). So retrosynthesis: maybe break amide via reverse of amide formation (i.e., disconnection to an acid and amine). Then break C-N bond from triazine to benzyl via SN2? Actually the bond is C-CH2-aryl attached to N of triazine (N-alkyl). Could be formed via SN2 of benzyl halide with triazine nitrogen. Then final step: Friedel-Crafts acylation to install amide carbonyl onto anisole? Wait amide attaches to anisole via anilide: anisidine (aniline) reacting with acyl chloride (the triazine carbonyl). So forward: Friedel-Crafts acylation? Actually Friedel-Crafts acylation attaches acyl to aromatic ring, but here we have anilide (aryl amide) not acylation of aromatic. Could be substitution of halogen on anisole with amide? Might be nucleophilic aromatic substitution? But guidance says forward reactions: Sn2, Friedel-Crafts acylation, substitution (hydroxyl to halogen). So we need to propose retrosynthetic steps corresponding to reverse of those: i.e., step1: break C-N bond formed by SN2 (reverse SN2) -> precursor: triazine with N-H (instead of N-alkyl) and benzyl halide (e.g., benzyl chloride). Step2: break amide bond formed by Friedel-Crafts acylation? Actually Friedel-Crafts acylation forms C-C bond, not amide. But maybe they intend acylation of anisole to give aryl ketone, then later convert to amide? Not sure.

Maybe simpler: propose three steps: 1) Disconnection of amide to give aniline (anisidine) and acyl chloride (triazine carbonyl chloride). 2) Disconnection of N-alkyl bond to give triazine with NH and benzyl chloride. 3) Disconnection of benzyl chloride to give phenyl ring with CH2OH (aliphatic hydroxyl) then substitution to halogen (Cl). So reverse of substitution: start from benzyl alcohol, convert to benzyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> step1 (reverse amide formation) -> precursors: anisidine (COc1cccc(NH2)c1) and acyl chloride: C(=O)Cl attached to triazine (ClC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N). Actually need to keep N-alkyl still present. So acyl chloride precursor still has N-alkyl side chain.

Step2: reverse SN2: acyl chloride precursor still has N-alkyl side chain attached via N-CH2-aryl. Break that to give triazine with NH (instead of N-CH2-aryl) and benzyl chloride (ClCH2c3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3). Step3: reverse substitution: benzyl chloride to benzyl alcohol (ClCH2-aryl -> HOCH2-aryl). So final precursors: anisidine, triazine with NH, benzyl alcohol, and maybe the azetidine side chain already present.

We need to ensure templates exist. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find templates for SN2 (functional_groups_broken: halide, formed: aliphatic halide? Actually SN2 forward: halide broken, C-N formed). So broken functional group: halide. Formed: aliphatic amine? Not sure.

Let's search.
